svg.title: Queue-Based Load Leveling
svg.desc: Queue-Based Load Leveling. A queue absorbs traffic spikes so the backend can work at a steady pace. Step 1, Without a queue: No queue: a spike of 15 requests/s hits a service that can do 5/s, so most calls time out. Step 2, Put a queue in between: The API puts each request on a queue and answers 202 at once; the worker pulls at its own pace. Step 3, The spike is absorbed: The spike is absorbed: the queue fills to 20 while the worker stays at 5/s. Nothing is dropped. Step 4, Drain, and know the limits: The queue drains in 10 s. It only moves load in time: cap it, watch depth and age, scale workers.

g.text: No queue: a spike of 15 requests/s hits a service that can do 5/s, so most calls time out.
The API puts each request on a queue and answers 202 at once; the worker pulls at its own pace.
The spike is absorbed: the queue fills to 20 while the worker stays at 5/s. Nothing is dropped.
The queue drains in 10 s. It only moves load in time: cap it, watch depth and age, scale workers.
scale out when depth or age stays high
direct call: every caller waits for the answer
of the 30 calls in the spike
cap the queue: when full, reject or shed
3 in, up to 5 out per second: the queue stays empty
a message arriving now waits 20 ÷ 5 = 4 s
alert on depth and on the age of the oldest message
if arrivals stay above 5/s, the backlog grows without end
spare capacity 5 − 3 = 2/s, so the 20 drain in 10 s
slow motion: the spike lasts 2 s
